sections.title: Page 13
sections.hint: Hams = whisper. With كۡ let a little air flow out, like a soft whisper. Middle or end of the word, the air still flows. At the end, stop softly — no bounce. Workbook Level 3, page 13 — Makharij & Sifat. Tap a form to hear it, then trace it on the page.

sections.title: Page 14
sections.hint: Hams = whisper. With تۡ let a little air flow out, like a soft whisper. Say تۡ softly with a little air — it is not a qalqala letter, so no bounce. Workbook Level 3, page 14 — Makharij & Sifat. Tap a form to hear it, then trace it on the page.

sections.title: Page 15
sections.hint: Heavy letters خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ: full, deep sound. With a kasra, خ غ ق get a little lighter. Kasra makes only خ غ ق less heavy. Fatha or damma keeps them fully heavy. Workbook Level 3, page 15 — Makharij & Sifat. Tap a form to hear it, then trace it on the page.

sections.title: Page 16
sections.hint: These never get lighter: ص ض ط ظ. Even صِ ضِ طِ ظِ stay fully heavy. Same deep sound in all three boxes. Workbook Level 3, page 16 — Makharij & Sifat. Tap a form to hear it, then trace it on the page.

sections.title: Page 17
sections.hint: The ل of ٱللَّه is heavy after fatha or damma (or when you start), light after kasra. Every other ل is light. لِلَّهِ is a short spelling: لِ + ٱللَّه. The ٱ and one ل are not written. Workbook Level 3, page 17 — Makharij & Sifat. Tap a form to hear it, then trace it on the page.

sections.title: Page 18
sections.hint: Heavy ر: full, deep sound. Light ر: thin sound. Read the rule above each table first. Workbook Level 3, page 18 — Makharij & Sifat. Tap a form to hear it, then trace it on the page.
